title: Gemini 4 is almost ready, says new Google DeepMind chief
content:
Google is reportedly nearing the launch of its long awaited Gemini 4 model, after dawdling behind rival developers on flagship AI releases. Speaking with The Information during his first media appearance as the leader of Google’s DeepMind division, Koray Kavukcuoglu said that Gemini 4 is currently in its refinement stage, and that the company is aiming to launch the model “much earlier” than the end of the year.
Gemini 4 is almost ready, says new Google DeepMind chief
The new frontier AI model should arrive long before the end of 2026.
“Our intention is to, like — as soon as possible — to release an early post-training output because we see the results and we are excited,” Kavukcuoglu told the publication, adding that Google would “continue the fast-paced iterations” going forward. This hopefully marks Google returning to a more consistent AI release timeline following a shakeup at DeepMind’s top leadership, with former AI head Demis Hassabis stepping down in August after announcing that “great progress” was being made on Gemini 4.
Google hasn’t released a new flagship AI model since the Gemini 3 series in November 2025. OpenAI’s GPT-6 and Anthropic’s Mythos series models have launched since then. Both outperform Gemini 3 and give the rival AI providers a sizable lead against Google in the AI race. Google CEO Sundar Pichai said at the I/O event in May that a major Gemini 3.5 Pro update would be coming in June to help bridge the gap, but the model was never rolled out.
Kavukcuoglu said the company “took a little bit of a step back” to focus on introducing faster, less powerful Flash models instead of releasing Gemini 3.5 Pro. When asked whether he was concerned about Google falling behind its rivals on AI development, he told The Information that “In my mind, it’s a certainty that we are always gonna be at the frontier.”

report.summary: New Google DeepMind chief Koray Kavukcuoglu says Gemini 4 is in refinement and will launch much earlier than year-end, as Google seeks to catch rivals.
report.background: Google has been under pressure in the frontier AI race since its last flagship model, the Gemini 3 series, arrived in November 2025. In the months that followed, rivals OpenAI and Anthropic shipped GPT-6 and the Mythos series, both of which reportedly outperform Gemini 3 and gave those providers a clear lead. Google CEO Sundar Pichai had said at I/O in May that a major Gemini 3.5 Pro update would arrive in June to close the gap, but it never launched. Instead, DeepMind prioritized faster, less powerful Flash models. The delay coincided with a leadership shakeup: Demis Hassabis stepped down in August after citing “great progress” on Gemini 4, and Koray Kavukcuoglu took over. Now Kavukcuoglu says Google is refining Gemini 4 and intends to ship an early post-training output as soon as possible.
key_points: Gemini 4 is currently in its refinement stage, according to Koray Kavukcuoglu. Google intends to release an early post-training output “as soon as possible” because internal results are exciting, and the company plans to continue fast-paced iterations. The model is expected to launch “much earlier” than the end of the year, signaling a return to a more consistent release cadence.

Google has not shipped a new flagship AI model since the Gemini 3 series in November 2025. Since then, OpenAI’s GPT-6 and Anthropic’s Mythos models have launched and outperform Gemini 3, giving Google’s rivals a sizable lead. A promised Gemini 3.5 Pro update in June never rolled out, deepening concerns about Google’s competitive position.

The delay followed a DeepMind leadership shakeup. Former AI head Demis Hassabis stepped down in August after announcing “great progress” on Gemini 4, and Koray Kavukcuoglu took over the division. In his first media appearance as leader, Kavukcuoglu said Google took a step back to prioritize faster, less powerful Flash models instead of releasing Gemini 3.5 Pro.

Kavukcuoglu remains confident about Google’s frontier position. When asked whether he worried about falling behind rivals, he said, “In my mind, it’s a certainty that we are always gonna be at the frontier.” The company aims to balance fast Flash releases with a major Gemini 4 launch to reassure developers and enterprise customers.
report.impact: For the AI industry, a near-term Gemini 4 would intensify the frontier model race and pressure OpenAI, Anthropic, and others to accelerate their own roadmaps. Google’s return could also shift pricing and capability benchmarks, especially if Gemini 4 narrows or closes the gap with GPT-6 and Mythos. Developers may benefit from another strong API option, potentially with competitive pricing, longer context, and tighter integration into Google Cloud, AI Studio, and Android. But the delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro and leadership changes may make some teams cautious about betting solely on Google. Regular users could see smarter Gemini assistants in Search, Workspace, and Android, plus faster Flash models for everyday tasks. However, launch timing remains uncertain, so users should treat the promise as a signal, not a guaranteed product date.
report.tools: To follow Gemini 4, watch Google AI Studio and Vertex AI Model Garden for early access and benchmarks, plus the Gemini API docs. For developers wanting provider flexibility, LiteLLM offers an open-source proxy to route across Gemini, OpenAI, and Anthropic; LangChain and LlamaIndex simplify switching models in apps. OpenRouter can help compare pricing and latency across frontier models. Also keep an eye on Google DeepMind’s blog and the Gemini app for consumer-facing updates.
